title: Scale the portions, not the pan
hook: A four-portion recipe uses 300g. How much corresponds to six portions?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

misconception: The same ingredient quantity serves more people without changing portion size.
objective: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

claims.text: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. Scaled model; quantities only; no cooking guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Portions=6, A=450g and B=300g. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; recall at x=9: B=300. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",75,"x"]; B=300; x denotes Portions. At x=6, A=450, B=300; recall at x=9: B=300. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. Change only Portions to 9. What is B (Unchanged) now? Correct: 300g. Use B's stated rule with Portions=9: it gives 300g. The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.

recall.question: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. Change only Portions to 9. What is B (Unchanged) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Portions=9: it gives 300g. The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.

safety.assumptions: The quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
